patch.value: Platform nightly legs regress after the shell-dialect rendering: Windows tests expect POSIX recovery text, and macOS bash 3.2 with history expansion misparses a rendered command at a non-ASCII apostrophe

The 2026-11-25 nightly (run 45629253836, commit b7356de67, the first main after the PowerShell and bash history-expansion rendering changes) failed on windows-latest shards 2, 3 and 4 and on macos-latest shard 1, so the aggregate ubuntu job failed too; the previous nightly on 6b998021d was green. Windows: recovery text is now rendered in the cmd dialect, for example ^"command=^<actual command^>,timeout_seconds=\^"90\^"^", while tests in linked-resource-admission.integration.spec.ts, linked-resource-recovery.spec.ts and register-commands.spec.ts expect the POSIX spelling command=<actual command>; these are platform-dependent expectations. macOS: rendered-command-shell-safety.integration.spec.ts 'posix: bash with history expansion on receives every argument literally' receives 25 arguments instead of 12, the parse breaking at the argument smart’s (U+2019), so a rendered command is not paste-safe under the system bash 3.2 with history expansion; this is a product defect, not only a test expectation. Linux passes both.

Windows recovery-text tests derive their expectations from the dialect renderer instead of a POSIX literal; The rendered-command safety test passes under bash 3.2 with history expansion, including non-ASCII arguments; A dispatched Nightly Validation run is green on every leg
Every nightly leg passes: Windows tests compare recovery text through the dialect renderer, and a rendered POSIX command survives bash 3.2 with history expansion byte for byte
Windows legs fail on POSIX-spelled expectations and the macOS leg receives 25 arguments instead of 12 from one rendered command
